chapter_theme: The order of the three gods (மும்மூர்த்திகளின் முறைமை): Siva is the one source, and Brahma and Vishnu are his aspects or parts, holding their place from him; those who split the three into rival gods and quarrel over them have not understood.
structure_note: Polemic verses against dividing the three (104, 107, 110) alternate with verses on how the one Lord takes on the three functions and forms (105, 106, 111, 112); 108 is Tirumular's own commission, 109 puts Siva's grace above every other god.

103.reading: For one who understands the measureless youth, end and limit, measured time and the four, Sankara is unwearied, and the measureless greatness his devotees speak of is what reaches Hari and Brahma.
103.nuance: The verse is compressed and its first two lines are obscure: நாலும் (the four) is unexplained, and அளவில் may mean 'measureless' or 'in measure'. The last line is commonly taken to mean that Hari and Brahma hold their greatness from Siva, which fits the chapter, but the syntax does not settle it.

104.reading: The first Lord, the one coloured like a fine jewel and the one on the petals of the first lotus are, on examination, one in their continuity; those who do not say so divide them and quarrel throughout the world.
104.nuance: ஆதிப் பிரான் is Siva, அணிமணி வண்ணன் Vishnu and the one on the lotus Brahma. தொடர்ச்சியில் ஒன்று (one in continuity) does not say the three are identical; it may mean they form one sequence or one lineage from a single source. பேதித்து பிணங்குதல names sectarian quarrelling.

105.reading: The Lord stands beyond the two kinds of deeds; the seed became the great god for the world; those who say the Lord is this or that have no understanding, while those who held fast knew the root.
105.nuance: இருவினை is good and bad deeds. பீசம் (bija, seed) is unclear: the Lord as seed of the world, or a seed-syllable. தூசு பிடித்தவர் (those who held the cloth) is taken as those who clung to the Lord as a child holds a garment's hem; தூர் (root, base) may be the Lord as source.

106.reading: With Siva first, the three and the five excel; from them come twelve, one joined with one; from them bindu and nada rise; and Sankara, first in the assembly, has these as his own name.
106.nuance: The numbers (three, five, twelve, one with one) are not explained in the verse. Tradition reads them as groups of deities or powers emanating from Siva, but which groups is not fixed by the text. The plain point is that every emanation, up to bindu and nada, is Siva's own name and form.

107.reading: Reckoning by that way, knowing the fruit, Brahma and Vishnu are not strangers to us; they are kin of three-eyed Nandi, and you will gain blessing through those gods.
107.nuance: வயனம் is obscure; it may stand for வசனம் (word) or a blessing. தமர் (one's own people) makes Brahma and Vishnu Siva's kin and so worthy of regard, not rivals. The verse accepts their worship within Siva's order.

108.reading: As I bowed and worshipped the milk-white one surrounded by his court of deathless gods, he said: 'You are equal to Mal and to Brahma; give our feet to the world.'
108.nuance: The speaker is taken to be Tirumular, and the verse as Siva's commission to him to teach. Who is 'equal to Mal and Brahma' is not wholly clear: it may be Tirumular, honoured as a teacher, or the phrase may compare Siva's gift. நம் அடி நல்கிடு, 'give our feet', makes the teaching the giving of Siva's feet.

109.reading: Whether gods or humans, there is no separate god to settle on and think of other than the grace of Siva of the honeyed konrai; it is that grace which knows those who dwell in flesh.
109.nuance: The verse puts grace (அருள்) in the place of a god: the only deity is Siva's grace. The last line can also be read as 'it is that which those in the body must come to know'.

110.reading: The ignorant do not know that the great light, examined, stood as three and as five in the beginning; they babble, dividing it into the Lord, tall Mal and Brahma by their functions.
110.nuance: மூன்று ஐந்து may be the three gods and the five (adding Maheswara and Sadasiva), or the five acts of the Lord. நீதிக்கண் is read here as 'by their offices'. ஆதர் means the blind or the ignorant; பிதற்றுதல் is a strong word for babbling.

111.reading: One in the supreme, inside and outside, becoming Vishnu and Brahma in their boons, taking many natures in their ranks, he stands concealed and works dissolution.
111.nuance: The verse gives the one Lord the three functions: preserving as Vishnu, creating as Brahma, dissolving himself. கரத்தினுள் is taken as 'in concealment' (from கர, hide); 'in the hand' is also possible. வரம் and தரம் (boon, rank) are uncertain.

112.reading: One part of him is Sadasiva our Lord; one part joins and stays in the sky; one part as lord stands in the body and gives it breath; and one part is the one of the waters.
112.nuance: சலமயன் (the one of water) is unclear: Vishnu lying on the waters, or Siva bearing the Ganga. The third line is the most important for the book as a whole: the Lord is the one who breathes in every body.

links.note: 112 names one part of the Lord as the one who stands in the body and breathes; 116 makes the body a temple where Nandi has taken up residence like fire latent in bamboo.

source_issues: 105: இருவினைககு is a misprint for இருவினைக்கு, and உலகல் is probably உலகில்.
107: நமககு is a misprint for நமக்கு; வயனம் is obscure and may be corrupt.
